big_idea: Geometers SORT solids, BUILD structures, MATCH congruent parts, and FOLLOW maps.
learning_intention: We are learning to sort, build, match, and follow movement directions.
student_learning_goal: I can sort, build, match, and follow movement directions.
success_criteria: I can SORT 4 solids by attribute.
I can FOLLOW a multistep direction.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Trekker Tig and Compass Coco — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.

minds_on.hook: Trekker Tig: Today's BIG case — sort, build, match, follow. The 4 detective tools of geometry! Tig + Coco open: 'SORT, COMPOSE, CONGRUENT, MAP — that's GEOMETRY!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Trekker Tig and Compass Coco puppets in capes. 'Geometer friends — today is our CAPSTONE. We use ALL we know: 5 solids, compose-decompose, congruent, and movement.'

Review the 4 detective steps: 'Step 1 — SORT 5 solids. Step 2 — COMPOSE/DECOMPOSE structures. Step 3 — MATCH congruent faces. Step 4 — FOLLOW movement directions.'

Demo each briefly:
- 'Sort: which solids have 6 faces? Cube, prism.'
- 'Compose: stack 3 = tower.'
- 'Match: 2 same squares = congruent.'
- 'Move: 3 steps + quarter turn = treasure.'

Now show the 4 stations:
- Station 1: SORT — name and count attributes for 4 solids.
- Station 2: BUILD — compose a 3-part structure.
- Station 3: MATCH — identify 3 congruent pairs.
- Station 4: FOLLOW — execute 2 multistep directions.

Each child rotates and records on TEMPLATE.

'Trekker Tig says — every BIG case uses all 4 tools!'

steps.instruction: Hand out templates. 4 stations rotation (~6 min each).
Stretch: write a 'geometer's brag': 1 sentence per station.
Help with quarter/half turn at Station 4.

STRATEGY COMPARE at Station 2 (BUILD) or Station 3 (MATCH): Two geometers use different congruence-checking approaches — overlay vs measure. Class compares accuracy. Cite Battista (2007) levels of geometric reasoning.
steps.teacher_prompt: Tig: 'Different methods, same answer. Pick the method your brain trusts.'

differentiation.for_movement_learners: Walk between 4 stations physically. NO-PREP VERSION: children rotate to 4 corners of the room — Sort corner, Compose corner, Congruent corner, Map corner. Body becomes the geometry workshop.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Four signals: sort; build; match; follow.

consolidation.activity_name: Tig and Coco's Big Map Brag
consolidation.exit_routine: Capstone refrain — Tig + Coco: 'SORT, COMPOSE, CONGRUENT, MAP — that's GEOMETRY!' Class chants 3x. Each child shares their case + the tool used at each step.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the geometer doesn't check their work — repairing the no-verify trap
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On the geometry capstone, the trap is single-skill fixation (uses only sort or only map) AND no-verify (doesn't check after solving). Battista's levels of geometric reasoning place verification as the L2→L3 transition target.

Today integrates Lessons 1-4: sort solids (L1), compose (L2), congruent (L3), map+move (L4) into a peer geometry case.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Capstone Station 1. Child writes 'cone has 5 vertices' without counting.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Trekker Tig asks — show me where each VERTEX is. Point.'

Guide. 'Apex — that's 1. Any others on a cone? No. So: 1 vertex.'

Generalise. 'Trekker Tig says — at G3, geometers always CHECK by counting or matching.'

If still rushed: pencil-touch each. 'Touch the vertex. Count out loud.'
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child uses only one prior-day skill: explicit checklist (sort, compose, congruent, map); child checks all four before final answer.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child solves but doesn't verify: force the verify step — 'check by overlaying / by recounting'.
DIAGNOSTIC C — child can verify but doesn't articulate: force 'I checked by ___ and confirmed ___.'

parts_outline.task: Sort 4 solids by attribute and name them.
Decompose 1 structure into its 3D parts and find 1 congruent pair.
Follow a 4-step direction on a map grid.
